sources.author: Dale J. Barr; Roger Levy; Christoph Scheepers; Harry J. Tily
sources.title: Random effects structure for confirmatory hypothesis testing: Keep it maximal
sources.inspected_scope: Author-hosted PDF title, abstract, and introduction explaining clustered observations, reader/participant and item variation, crossed random effects, and design-based specification. Also inspected pp. 258-259 discussion of random intercepts and random slopes. Did not audit the complete simulation results or reproduce them.
sources.locator: Journal of Memory and Language 68, pp. 255-259; PDF pp. 1-5
sources.limitations: The paper primarily addresses linear mixed models. It does not validate this project's as-yet-unbuilt ordinal instrument or determine its eventual random-effects structure. Its maximal-model recommendation is not presented as an unqualified rule for every dataset.
supports: Repeated responses can cluster by participants and linguistic materials
Generalization depends on modeling variation across both readers and passages
Variation in manipulation effects may require random slopes

sources.author: Andrew Gelman; Eric Loken
sources.title: The garden of forking paths: Why multiple comparisons can be a problem, even when there is no fishing expedition or p-hacking and the research hypothesis was posited ahead of time
sources.inspected_scope: Author-hosted paper dated 14 November 2013; abstract and Sections 1.1-1.2, including distinction between a fixed analysis, a prespecified analysis choice, data-dependent choices, and explicit fishing.
sources.limitations: Methodological argument, not a study of Quranic numerical claims. Chapter's application to spelling, tokenization, and boundary choice is the project's own proposed application. The paper is cited as the dated author-hosted manuscript, not assigned an invented journal citation.
supports: Data-dependent analytical paths can create a multiplicity problem even when one final analysis is performed
Sincere analysis does not remove selection effects
